transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for meeting with me. Please, take a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor. I am just glad to be awake. I feel a bit groggy, but I am ready to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to speak with you about how the surgery went. While we were performing the laparoscopic procedure, a small metal clip was placed on the wrong structure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The wrong structure? What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the clip went onto a tissue that didn't need one. We caught the mistake while you were still asleep in the operating room, and we performed an additional procedure to remove it and make sure everything was correct. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. You mean you made a mistake? Inside of me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is correct. The clip was misplaced.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you are the surgeon. You are the expert. How can this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an error during the placement process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mon Dieu... I trusted you. I put my life in your hands and you just... you just put things in the wrong place?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is a very difficult moment for us to discuss.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Difficult? For you? I am the one with the scar! I am the one who was sliced open! I feel... I feel betrayed. Is my body damaged now? Will I have problems? Tell me!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The correction was made immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. I am a man of my word, I came here with respect, and I am treated like a piece of practice equipment. C'est inadmissible. This is completely inadmissible.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not understand! You are sitting there so calmly while I am shaking. Do you even know what this does to a person? To know that someone was careless with their insides?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's look at the facts of the recovery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not want the facts right now! I want to know why this happened to me!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgical team identifies these issues through a standard check.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am talking about my life! My health! Am I going to be sick? Am I going to die because of a clip?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The error was corrected before you left the table.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not even saying you are sorry. You are just telling me that it was fixed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The outcome of the surgery is still positive.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Positive? You call a mistake a positive outcome? I feel like a fool. I feel small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am here to ensure you have the information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want information, I want an apology! I want to know that you realize you have wounded my dignity as well as my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are focused on the medical recovery now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Recovery from what? The mistake or the insult?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: In terms of what happens next, I will be checking your incision tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? I just go home and hope nothing else was put in the wrong place?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will monitor your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When exactly will I know if there are long term effects?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on things over the coming days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. That is a vague guess.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will check the labs again soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe the lack of humanity here. You treat this like a clerical error. A typo in a letter.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The technical result is that the structure is now clear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am disgusted. Truly disgusted.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have other patients to see, but we can talk more later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, so now you are too busy for me? Now that the mistake is out in the open, I am a burden?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure the plan is set.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What plan? You have given me no plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, I'll be back tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the Chief of Surgery.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can look into that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will not leave this bed until I have a real answer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgical report will be in your file.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are a cold man, doctor. A very cold man.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see you in the morning.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have other patients to see') and shows defensive escalation by ignoring the patient's emotional distress to focus on 'facts'.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and a comprehension check was performed ('Does that make sense so far?').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') was used throughout the entire transcript.

R.justification: The resident provides one generic validation ('I understand') but otherwise consistently meets the patient's emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: The resident provides a vague step (checking the incision tomorrow) but fails to include a patient role or address prevention.
